text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The tempo in the fight for control of Zimbabwe's second cellular phone network moved a notch up this week, with revelations that President Robert Mugabe had ordered the information ministry to issue an operating licence to embattled local entrepreneur Strive Masiyiwa.
- The government has virtually concluded plans to take over half of Lonrho Zimbabwe's multi-billion-dollar investments, sources in Harare and London told the Financial Gazette this week.
- South Africa said on Wednesday it had offered neighbouring Zimbabwe a list of primary agricultural products which the latter could export at lower tariffs.

- Zimbabwean commercial banks have turned down an offer by the Reserve Bank to disburse the World Bank's Z$830 million loan facility for small-to-medium-scale businesses, saying the target group was "risky" and the funds were open to political interference.
- Zimbabwe's tax department has unearthed an Z$80 million evasion case involving a well-known public organisation in the capital Harare.
- An initial 200 workers will be re-employed at textile firm Cone Textiles' Norton subsidiary next month when the company resumes operations after being liquidated three years ago.

- Several top posts have been abolished at a leading Zimbabwean pharmaceutical firm, Datlabs Ltd, and many more are on the line in a major restructuring exercise ordered by its parent company, South Africa's Adcock Ingram Group.

- Zimbabwe's economy, now ripe for more foreign investment, is firmly on a positive growth path with effective measures being taken to contain public expenditure and collect all state revenue, President Robert Mugabe said in London on Wednesday.

- Prospects for a bilateral trade agreement between Zimbabwe and South Africa are gloomy, with the latter continuing to throw spanners in the works, Zimbabwe's industry and commerce minister Nathan Shamuyarira said on Wednesday.
- Interest among French companies willing to invest in Zimbabwe is expected to increase as a result of President Robert Mugabe's two-day visit to the European country starting Thursday.
